split.title: One tone in, two tones out
split.caption: Top: the 1,000 Hz tone splits into two half-size tones. Bottom: a whole voice splits into a wanted copy and a ghost that overlap almost everywhere, so no filter can pull them apart.

negative-tone.title: Two arrows, one shadow
negative-tone.caption: The top arrow is +1,000 Hz, the mirror arrow is the negative tone, −1,000 Hz. Sample by sample they cast the same shadow, so on the line they sound the same.

chip-boundary.title: Arrows inside, shadows outside
chip-boundary.caption: Inside the chip a sample can be an arrow, two numbers. Only what goes out on the line has to be a shadow.

ghost-arrows.title: The mirror arrow is the ghost
ghost-arrows.caption: One arrow turning +300 Hz adds 13.5° per sample to both arrows. The top arrow speeds up to 1,300 Hz; the mirror slows to −700 Hz, and its shadow is the 700 Hz ghost.

analytic.title: The analytic signal: the dot itself
analytic.caption: The analytic signal of one tone is the dot: its left-right part is the cosine you store, its up-down part the sine you need. That sine is the left-right part of the dot a quarter turn behind.

hilbert.title: Two quarter turns cancel the mirror
hilbert.caption: Follow the mirror arrow: the filter turns it a quarter turn forward, j turns it another, and it ends exactly opposite where it started. Added to the original, it cancels; the top arrow doubles.

delay-vs-quarter-turn.title: A delay is not a quarter turn
delay-vs-quarter-turn.caption: Top row: a delay turns each tone in proportion to its pitch. Bottom row: the Hilbert transformer turns every tone by the same quarter turn.

shifter.title: The single-sideband shifter
shifter.caption: Two multiplications and a subtraction per sample. The delay box keeps the plain path in step with the Hilbert transformer.

sideband.title: Single sideband keeps one copy
sideband.caption: A plain multiplication makes both sidebands. Single sideband keeps the upper one, 1,300 Hz, and removes the lower one, the ghost.

hilbert-response.title: The Hilbert transformer’s response
hilbert-response.caption: Every positive tone is turned back a quarter turn (−j, down), every negative tone forward (+j, up). The real 31-coefficient filter cannot jump at 0 Hz; it ramps.

h-sketch.title: Where 2 ÷ (πn) comes from
h-sketch.caption: Each coefficient is the average of sin(ωn) from 0 to π. Even n: the half-waves cancel. Odd n: one upward half-wave is left over.

taps.title: The Hilbert transformer’s coefficients
taps.caption: The ideal coefficients shrink like 1 ÷ n and reach backwards. Keep n from −15 to 15, taper them with the Hann window, and delay the list 15 samples.

delay-catch.title: The missing delay box
delay-catch.caption: Without the delay box, the mirror arrow no longer cancels. The ghost depends on the tone, and it is never small for long.

edges.title: Where a short Hilbert transformer fails
edges.caption: Top: the gain of the 31-coefficient Hilbert transformer. Bottom: the ghost it leaves. Both fail near 0 Hz, and at 300 Hz both miss the 5% target.
